name: Bajaj Auto Ltd
title: Bajaj Auto Ltd - 532977 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Record Q1 FY27 with EBITDA INR3,596 crore (20.9% margin) despite ~4.5% of revenue commodity inflation; capacity is now the binding constraint, with expansion from 7 to 9 million units announced.

summary.headline: Bajaj Auto Q1 FY27 revenue crossed INR17,000 crore (INR17,244 cr, +37% YoY) with EBITDA of INR3,596 cr at 20.9% margin despite ~4.5% commodity inflation.
summary.overview: Standalone volumes hit a record over 1.4 million units (+29% YoY) and PAT was a tad under INR3,000 crore (+42% YoY), with EBITDA margin up 10 bps QoQ and 110 bps YoY. Management said ransomware, LPG curtailment, West Asia logistics issues and labour shortages cost about 10% of volume, and that the company was tracking above 1.5 million units before these disruptions. Commodity inflation of about 4.5% of revenue was only about half offset by pricing, with the balance absorbed by a weaker rupee (realised USD-INR 94.4 vs 85.6 a year ago), mix and discretionary cost cuts. Management flagged broader cost inflation (proprietary parts, electronics, logistics, labour, energy) that Q2 will reflect more fully, and declined to quantify it.

financial_highlights.change: Expected to rebuild to ~INR15,000 crore by FY-end after July outflows
+65% YoY (includes full quarter of Bajaj Mobility AG; not like-for-like)
vs INR90.6 QoQ and INR85.6 YoY

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Record 732,000 units and USD 735 million revenue; about 40% of revenue. Growing over 2x the industry across top-30 markets except MENA; Africa retail doubled with ~60% retail share in Nigeria; three-wheeler exports hit 100,000 units (+~70%) with over 65% share.

segments.name: Domestic motorcycles
segments.commentary: Motorcycles ~25% of revenue. Industry motorcycle growth ~7-8% in Q1; Bajaj 150cc-plus outperforming industry by 1.5x with N and NS series ~60% of 150cc-plus sales, but 100cc and 125cc share is falling.

segments.name: Pro-Biking (KTM and Triumph)
segments.commentary: Nearly 40,000 domestic motorcycles, +50%+ YoY; KTM exports from India +20%+ and Triumph exports +40%; about 90 joint KTM-Triumph stores operational.

segments.name: Electric (Chetak and e-3W)
segments.commentary: EV two- and three-wheelers at ~30% of domestic revenue with double-digit EBITDA; Chetak volumes +65% YoY (industry ~+70%), first EBITDA-positive quarter; EV scooter capacity ~50,000 units/month, targeting ~60,000 near term.

segments.name: Three-wheelers (ICE and e-autos)
segments.commentary: ICE three-wheeler share ~70%; e-autos doubled and are 44% of L5 segment; Q1 record billings and retail; capacity constraints limited sales of some models.

segments.name: Spares
segments.commentary: Run-rate of INR1,700-1,800 crore in Q1 with record margins.

segments.name: Bajaj Auto Credit (BACL)
segments.commentary: Total income over INR1,100 crore; PAT INR227 crore (more than doubled YoY); AUM ~INR20,000 crore (+70%+ YoY); CRAR 19%; ROE over 25%.

segments.name: KTM AG
segments.commentary: First full quarter of line-by-line consolidation; production ramp-up and dealer/plant inventory normalisation largely complete; fixed-cost control improving.

guidance_outlook: Exports to move beyond 250,000 units per month from this quarter onward (was ~200,000 a few quarters ago).
Capacity expansion of ~25%, from ~7 million to 9 million+ units per annum over the medium term, focused on EVs (two- and three-wheeler), high-end motorcycles and wide-body three-wheelers.

Pulsar 150cc refresh and ~10 facelifts in 160-400cc and a new 125cc Pulsar to roll out over the next ~6 weeks (from 1 August); two new brands in 125cc planned within FY27 (timing subject to environment).
Q2 expected to see easing supply chain disruption (top-line support) but fuller impact of broader cost inflation; management declined to quantify.
Discretionary and fixed costs to be kept tight in Q2; marketing and launch spend not to be cut.
Payout: 100% of FY26 profit (INR9,825 crore) committed via base dividend plus buyback, with July outflow of ~INR10,000 crore.
capex_capacity: Current capacity ~7 million units per annum across businesses, expanding to 9 million+ units in the medium term (work already started).
EV two-wheeler (Chetak) capacity ~50,000 units/month, expected to rise to ~60,000 through productivity gains with vendors.
Three-wheeler capacity constraints in both ICE and electric (EV 7012 wide-body described as top-selling model); capacity unlocking underway without a stated number.
Chetak exclusive store network 530+ stores, 4,500 touchpoints in 850+ cities; target of ~1,000 stores in a couple of years.
Ransomware-related suspension of operations for a few days in Q1; availability hit 10-15% in exports, high-end bikes and EVs.
demand_pricing: Two-wheeler industry registrations +14% YoY in Q1 (vs ~25% in Q4); motorcycles +7-8%; 100cc and 125cc flat to low single digit; 150cc-plus and 250cc growing 20%+; EV scooters ~+67-70%, EV penetration ~25% of scooters all-India.
Commodity inflation ~4.5% of revenue in Q1 (vs 3.5-4% guided in May); steel +10%+, aluminium and platinum ~+40%, rhodium ~+40%.
Pricing taken in April and June offset about half of commodity inflation.
Management says 100cc share has fallen (55% to ~45% of motorcycles over several years) and it will prioritise profitability there, accepting share loss.
E-rick (L3) market ~45,000 units/month, ~90% lead acid; migration to lithium expected; loan access remains a constraint.
Management says it is losing discretionary-cost leverage risk in Q2 due to inflation; other expenses fell as a % of sales QoQ and YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why are sub-125cc motorcycles weak despite GST cut, and is there a shift from ICE to EV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is split by income segment: 150cc-plus growing 20%+ while 100cc and 125cc grow low single digits. EV two-wheelers are up ~67-70%, driven by fuel-cost concerns after West Asia/LPG issues, cannibalising ICE scooters most.

qa_highlights.question: What are EV capacity plans and where is EV profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Two-wheeler EV capacity at 50,000 units, targeting 60,000 near term; three-wheeler capacity also constrained. EV portfolio EBITDA is double digit, and Chetak has turned EBITDA positive (earlier neutral).

qa_highlights.question: Confirm the launch roadmap and whether there are new nameplates.
qa_highlights.answer: About 10 Pulsar facelifts and a new 150cc Pulsar within ~6 weeks from 1 August; new 125cc Pulsar to follow; two new brands in 125cc (not Pulsar-named) planned within FY27, timing dependent on environment.

qa_highlights.question: Is the market share decline a strategic choice toward premium?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wholesale share is affected by stock policy and Vahan is the better yardstick. 100cc share loss is deliberate to protect profitability; 150cc-plus share is rising, and the same is expected in 125cc after launches.

qa_highlights.question: Is other expenses ratio sustainable and what about cash deployment?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said discretionary and fixed costs will stay tight in Q2, while marketing spend will not be cut. Cash of ~INR21,000 crore falls after ~INR10,000 crore July outflow, then rebuilds to ~INR15,000 crore by FY-end; base dividend plus buyback chosen for tax reasons.

qa_highlights.question: What is the KTM-Bajaj manufacturing and R&D collaboration?
qa_highlights.answer: KTM is run independently; co-design and manufacturing in India for smaller-capacity KTM bikes is being restarted, with India expected to carry substantial manufacturing but not become a global hub. Triumph has ~210-215 outlets including ~90 joint stores.

risks_watch: Broader cost inflation (components, electronics, logistics, labour, energy) hitting Q2 margins; company declined to size it and said estimates could change weekly.
Rupee tailwind may fade, depending on RBI measures and currency path.
Continued 100cc share loss and whether the new 125cc launches and new brands recover share.
Supply constraints in EVs and three-wheelers and the pace of capacity to 9 million units.
KTM turnaround and consolidation effects, which make consolidated comparisons not like-for-like.
Consumer stress in lower-income segments; LPG and fuel availability.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and exports and on the product reset, but cautious on cost outlook: management repeatedly said the environment is volatile and declined to quantify Q2 inflation. Some Q&A answers on motorcycle strategy were deliberately long and evasive on launch timing.
key_quotes: It was a tough quarter with RM inflation, supply chain and logistics disruptions as well as a ransomware attack, which you may have read about, but it was defended comprehensively and successfully.
It was clearly a hyperinflationary commodity environment with virtually the entire basket witnessing sharp increases.
Capacities have emerged as a key constraint to growth.
Capacity is just table stakes. I mean if you can't manufacture, then you can't sell.

adds.what: Capacity expansion ~25%, from ~7M to 9M+ units per annum across businesses (EVs 2W/3W, high-end motorcycles, wide-body 3W)
EV two-wheeler (Chetak) capacity rising from ~50,000 to ~60,000 units/month via productivity gains with vendors
Pulsar 150cc refresh, ~10 facelifts and new 125cc Pulsar rolling out from 1 August

growth.why: Management guides exports beyond 250,000 units/month from Q2 and a ~25% capacity expansion (7M to 9M+ units) over the medium term, with Chetak capacity to ~60,000/month immediately, but no revenue growth % is guided, the 9M expansion has no stated capex or timing, and Q2 cost inflation is unquantified.
